label: Unvalidated PitchIQ rules; review with a coach.
about: The mastery rules of PitchIQ coaching v2 progression (DESIGN v2 section 8.4), read by soccer/coaching/progress.py. Every number is a PitchIQ proposal: no federation source gives a threshold for when a team has mastered a positional behaviour, and no coach has labelled a match yet. States are computed per skill from opportunities (moments where the behaviour mattered), never from match totals or report wording.

interval.basis: DESIGN 8.4: Wilson score interval at 80% (two-sided) on the share of judged opportunities that demonstrated the behaviour.

evidence.basis: DESIGN 8.4: a match qualifies with at least 6 judged opportunities; NOT ENOUGH EVIDENCE below 20 judged opportunities or 2 qualifying matches; CONSISTENT reads the last 3 qualifying matches. The window (the most recent 5 qualifying matches and every match after the first of them) and the quality floor (identity and position at least medium, as the report's guardrails ask of a criticism) are PitchIQ additions.

thresholds.basis: DESIGN 8.4: s1 is the lower bound for DEVELOPING and the per-match share every one of the last qualifying matches needs for CONSISTENT; s2 the lower bound for CONSISTENT and for each context of ADAPTABLE.

adaptable.basis: DESIGN 8.4: CONSISTENT in at least 2 contexts with at least 6 judged opportunities each. Contexts: the ball's third (zone), the ball's channel, the wide defender's side, the match format.

trend.basis: The latest qualifying match against the up to 3 qualifying matches before it, per opportunity: a change of at least 0.1 in the share that a two-proportion test also finds at 90% (two-sided); otherwise flat. 90% and not the states' 80%: a trend claims a change between matches, and at 80% one comparison in five of a team that did not change would show one (on Metrica game 1 cut into 15-minute parts, 80% read 'down' for pressure and cover at 7 of the 14 team x level readings, 90% at 1).

rates.basis: Rates are per 10 minutes of the skill's relevant phase (DESIGN 8.4), so a 60 s clip and a 90 minute match are compared per opportunity and per phase minute, never on totals; a range under 3 minutes is called a short clip in the note.
